I stopped to take a leak at the local (very small and sleepy) mall. I pulled up to the small side entrance where the bathrooms are. The walk to the door is flanked by brown mulch. It's hot today, and breezy. Great fire weather. Someone apparently tossed a still smoldering butt into the mulch. I parked, and saw a little plume of white smoke billowing from the mulch bed.

At this point, I would like to point out something that seems really obvious in hindsight: when you have a situation like this, it's a lot easier to keep the embers together in one spot. Well, I didn't do that. I thought I could get them up on the concrete and separate them from the rest of the kindling. That was a mistake. A store employee happened by. "Is it a cigarette?" she asked. "I'll be it was a cigarette."

"Probably," I say.

"I'll call someone," she said, and walked (walked) back inside. I run to my car to get the bucket of (soapy) water I have with me, because I wash windows for a living. 10 minutes go by with me stomping out any flames that appear, and another older women comes out. "You all set?" she asks.

"No, I'm not all set! The mulch is catching fire! I need water. Maybe the janitorial staff." My thinking was that this was an easily solved problem. We just needed a couple dozen gallons of water to douse the mulch bed. The janitor probably had a water key for the hose bib that was just inside the door. I could use my bucket and soak the mulch.

"We don't have a janitor at [store]." I just looked at her, probably visibly annoyed. "Maybe security?"

"Call security." And I continue stomping out the embers. At this point, the smoldering mulch is spread around the mulch bed pretty well, because I wasn't thinking clearly at first. I just saw fire and reacted. So I'm playing a game of whack-a-flame. Another 20 minutes of this, no sign of mall security. I run into [store], and the lady from before is calmly doing something behind the counter. "I just need some water," I said.

"Well, our bathrooms are all the way at the other end of the store..."

"No, I need something that can put out a few gallons of water quickly."

"Oh, like a hose or something?" She turned into Consuela, "Oh, no, no, no..."

"I'll just call the fire department." And I jog back outside.
